method: Three fresh reviewers each round, given only the eight blind sheets (docs/shipkit-15/blind/<surface>.jpg) and the cards' level descriptions (textures_1797.json), put each sheet's letters A to E in level order (each level once) and named the least convincing thing on each sheet. Rule (wear_check.py): a reviewer passes a surface with all five right or one swap of neighbouring levels; a surface passes when at least three reviewers do.

least_convincing.paint: L1 and L0 are almost the same; the salt streaks and loss of gloss barely show, and L3's touch-up patches read as blotchy grey stains, not glossier paint.
least_convincing.copper: L1's even brown is close to L3's dark old sheets; only the bright inset sheets mark L3.
least_convincing.wood: New, first cruise and kept oak differ only by a slight greying.
least_convincing.deck: New yellow pine and the scrubbed deck are nearly the same colour; new pine should be clearly yellower.
least_convincing.rope: The hemp falls look the same pale grey in all five panels and there is no glossy black tar anywhere.
least_convincing.canvas: L0, L1 and L3 sails are nearly identical; none looks like new buff flax.
least_convincing.iron: The L0 and L3 guns are the same, and L1's first orange bloom is invisible.
least_convincing.bright: L0 and L1 gilt are almost the same.

least_convincing.paint: L1's salt streaks are faint, and the glossy touch-up patches are the only thing that sets L3 apart from L0.
least_convincing.copper: L0 reads orange-tan rather than salmon-pink, and L1 is a reddish brown rather than an even warm brown.
least_convincing.wood: The oak's grain standing proud at L3 can't be seen.
least_convincing.deck: L3's white deck hides the hard seams.
least_convincing.rope: No fresh black tar on the falls.
least_convincing.canvas: The sails look nearly the same at every level.
least_convincing.iron: The gun looks the same smooth blacking at L0, L1 and L3.
least_convincing.bright: The gilt looks equally bright at L0, L1 and L3.

least_convincing.paint: A (L1) is hard to tell from new: the salt streaks under the ports barely show.
least_convincing.copper: C (L1) looks orange, nearly salmon, and D (L0) looks redder and darker.
least_convincing.wood: The new oak and the greying oak look almost the same.
least_convincing.deck: The L0 deck is pale tan rather than clearly yellow new pine.
least_convincing.rope: The tar looks almost identical at L0, L1, L3.
least_convincing.canvas: The sails for L0, L1 and L3 are nearly identical.
least_convincing.iron: No brown edges and no orange bloom on L1.
least_convincing.bright: The gilt looks about the same at L0, L1 and L3.

earlier_rounds.1: paint, rope pass; copper, canvas, bright, wood, deck, iron fail (mostly first cruise taken for thirty years kept)
earlier_rounds.2: paint, deck, rope, canvas, iron pass; copper, wood, bright fail (first cruise and thirty years kept swapped)
earlier_rounds.3: wood, deck, iron pass; paint, copper, rope, canvas, bright fail (the same swap)
earlier_rounds.4: deck, rope, canvas, iron pass; wood missed by one reviewer; paint, copper, bright fail: the cards' first-cruise copper ('a few sheets brighter') described the kept ship's renewed sheets, and new copper read orange

sheets_note: the SHA-256 of each blind sheet the round's reviewers saw (wear_check.py --sheets, seed 11, from the renders of docs/shipkit-15): the blind check fails on any other sheets
